r0-context.title: Load baseline context
r0-context.imperative: Read inherited global doctrine (reviewer references/global-crew.md and references/global-everyone.md), then project deltas if present: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, plus the g4 handoff, the g4 implementer handoff and result, and the diff. Record pass when loaded.
r0-context.finding: Loaded global-crew.md + global-everyone.md, docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md (python not py; never compare working-tree bytes on Windows; checklists only via engine verbs), GLOSSARY.md, the g4 reviewer handoff, the g4 implementer handoff (frozen falsifier list), the g4 implementer result, and the branch diff (main...f8b0743).

r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the g4 acceptance run do what the implementer handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: The gate delivered what the g4 implementer handoff asked. Vehicle: headless 'claude -p' with cwd in a disposable sandbox and a settings file wiring PostToolUse to this worktree's two hooks by absolute path - I read both settings files and both launch commands. Six agents actually ran (parent + ALPHA + BRAVO + CHARLIE + DELTA + depth-2 ECHO), matching the required run shape including the non-claiming subagent and the nested dispatch. HARD was reached on real reading (0.329482 of a 1M window), not SOFT. At least one agent released (ECHO, wk-echo lease=released, its composite key absent from the store). The sandbox had its own .agent-work/.spine-rail-binding.json and I confirmed the main checkout's live store holds 6 keys, none referencing accept419 and none composite - constraint 7 honored. identity_resolution_ms present on all three dispatched records (0.0776-0.0837 ms, inside the 100ms budget).

r2-scope.title: Scope drift
r2-scope.imperative: Confirm nothing outside .agent-work/ entered the diff at g4, and that the acceptance harness lives outside the repo and is uncommitted. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r2-scope.finding: In scope. 'git status --porcelain' filtered to exclude .agent-work paths returns empty - nothing outside .agent-work/ is uncommitted. The tracked main...HEAD diff touches docs/GAUGE_WRITER_HOOK.md, scripts/gauge_reader.py, scripts/hooks/{gauge_writer_hook,spine_rail}.py and tests/, all of which are g1-g3 commits already reviewed and closed; g4 added no source change. The acceptance harness lives outside the repo at scratchpad/accept419/ and never entered the diff - I confirmed it on disk. One cosmetic note: the g4 implementer plan's engine side-dirs landed at .agent-work/issue-419-governor-identity-g4/ (a sibling of the issue workbench) whereas g1-g3 review side-dirs landed inside .agent-work/issue-419-governor-identity/. Still under .agent-work/, so not a scope breach - recorded as an observation for closeout.

r3-evidence.title: Required evidence present and sufficient
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present, complete, and does it actually demonstrate a live per-agent trip? Enumerate the evidence set and check for gaps. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Evidence present and sufficient, with one hygiene defect. All items the handoff's 'Required evidence' list names are archived: both settings files, both launch commands, both arms' stdout, both binding stores, every gauge.json and every gauge-skip.json, both arms' full transcript sets (6 files each, byte sizes matching the live session dirs exactly), both recomputation scripts and their outputs, all 8 spines + journals, the agent_id grep, and the pre-run emptiness check. I re-ran recompute.py (exit 0) and its output is byte-identical to the archive. DEFECT: g4-assert-control-output.txt does NOT reproduce from g4-assert_control.py - the archived output carries a trailing 8-line section ('what the control arm's agents ACTUALLY consumed') that the archived script contains no code to emit, so it was appended from an unrecorded command. Not fatal: I independently recomputed every number in that section from the control transcripts and all five match (ALPHA 0.329265, BRAVO 0.102895, CHARLIE 0.062080, DELTA 0.027522, ECHO 0.065880). Recorded as an in-scope observation, not a blocker.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the g4 work meet inherited doctrine: fail-visibly, scoped nulls, claims pinned to a revision, side-effects verified against the world? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: Meets inherited doctrine. Fail-visibly: the control arm's hooks wrote gauge-skip.json records naming 'ambiguous-binding' with candidate_count rather than silently writing nothing - the blindness is legible on disk, which is what made the negative control readable at all. Scoped nulls: the 'what I deliberately did not do' section names concurrency, CI wiring and the unresolvable-identity case as untested, with reasons, and the run-1 discard is disclosed rather than buried. Claims pinned: the result names branch, HEAD, exact agent ids, exact session uuids and exact timestamps, so every number is re-derivable - I re-derived them. Side-effects verified against the world: I did not take the report's word for anything - the live sandbox and the live ~/.claude/projects session dirs are both still on disk and I read them directly. Honest self-correction is visible twice: the first pairing draft compared transcript tails and self-reported a false mismatch before being pinned to observed_at, and the first control assertion exited 1 on an over-broad claim and was tightened rather than weakened (I read the corrected script; it asserts strictly more).

r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from recorded architecture (docs/GAUGE_WRITER_HOOK.md, map) in a way Commander must reconcile? Verify the implementer's Map Impact notes against the diff and evidence. Record pass/fail; flag triage candidates.
r5-reconciliation.finding: No divergence needing rework; one doc-reconcile candidate. The implementer's Map Impact notes check out against the diff and the evidence: it claims no source file changed (git confirms g4 added nothing tracked), names the exact anchors exercised (spine_rail.binding_key/handle_post_tool_use, gauge_writer_hook._binding_key/derive_subagent_transcript/find_latest_usage/handle_post_tool_use, checklist_engine._trip_advisory/_trip_hard_gate) and I traced the observed behavior through each, and it correctly moves the 100ms identity-resolution budget from assumed to measured (0.0776-0.0837 ms on the live records). RECONCILE CANDIDATE: docs/GAUGE_WRITER_HOOK.md says nothing about nested dispatch - grep for depth/nested/spawnDepth returns only two unrelated hits - yet g4 established a new durable fact: a depth-2 agent's transcript is written directly under the ROOT session's subagents/ directory (I read agent-acbcb46bdf651a3c7.meta.json: spawnDepth 2, parentAgentId a3ab804c97222f9c5), which is exactly why derive_subagent_transcript resolves at depth 2. The implementer surfaced this as a Map Impact decision candidate rather than editing the doc, which is correct under g4's scope - it needs to reach Cartographer, not to block this gate. Second, smaller: the implementer flags that the map-anchors packet context/g4-implement.json has an empty files list, so Map Impact was written from the code rather than from the packet.

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass over the g4 acceptance harness and the shipped hook diff. Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell: flagged / overridden / absent. Record to FOWLER_PASS.json, run verify_fowler_pass.py, then record pass/fail.
constraints: Fowler smells are subordinate to documented repo standards; never hard violations
an override needs a logged reason
r6-fowler.finding: Pass run over the g4 work product - the 5-script, 828-line acceptance harness, since g4 ships no source diff. Record at .agent-work/issue-419-governor-identity/g4-review/FOWLER_PASS.json; verify_fowler_pass.py exits 0 (smells=12, flagged=[duplicated-code, data-clumps, shotgun-surgery], overridden=[long-method]). Three flags share one root: the arm concept (arm name, sandbox dir, settings, prompt, projects slug) is re-derived in each script instead of living in one place, which is why check() and slug_for() are copied and why a layout change would touch all five files. Raised as an observation for Commander, not a blocker - the harness is uncommitted and outside the repo by the handoff design, but it is archived as reusable evidence and the next acceptance run will fork it. long-method on recompute.py main() is overridden with a logged standard: the printed statement order IS the archived evidence artifact, and global-crew minimal-change plus the handoff throwaway-harness instruction subordinate the smell. The hook diff itself was Fowler-passed at g1-g3 and is closed; I did not re-pass it.

f1-key-shape.title: Falsifier 1 — binding key is bare, not composite
f1-key-shape.imperative: Inspect the treatment binding store. Confirm the dispatched agents' binding keys are <uuid>#<hex> composite, not bare. FIRES (fail) if bare.
f1-key-shape.finding: DID NOT FIRE. Read live at sandbox/.agent-work/.spine-rail-binding.json. Three keys: one bare 'e0063a6f-5f31-473e-938a-1feea2863166' holding only wk-parent, and two composite - '...#a6df3902f0bf72c29' -> wk-alpha and '...#a69093b8ea2f159f6' -> wk-bravo. My own regex check confirms each composite is <36-char uuid>#<lowercase hex>, that the uuid segment equals the counted session dir name on disk, and that each hex segment has its own agent-<id>.jsonl in that session's subagents/ directory.

f2-distinct-fills.title: Falsifier 2 — the two agents' fills match
f2-distinct-fills.imperative: Recompute both dispatched agents' fills from raw transcripts by your own route. FIRES (fail) if they match each other.
f2-distinct-fills.finding: DID NOT FIRE. Recomputed by my own parser from each agent's own transcript: ALPHA 0.329482 (329482 tokens), BRAVO 0.102211 (102211 tokens). Not equal, and not equal by a factor either. Peak fills across the whole run also differ (ALPHA 0.330102, BRAVO 0.102629), so the divergence is a property of what each agent actually read, not of a single sampling instant.

f3-pairing.title: Falsifier 3 — the pairing is crossed (THE decisive check)
f3-pairing.imperative: For each agent id, independently recompute the fill from that id's own agent-<id>.jsonl and confirm it matches the gauge.json in the spine directory that the SAME id's composite binding key points at. Do not import the hook under test; do not rely on the implementer's checker alone. STATE THE COUNT. FIRES (fail) on any cross.
f3-pairing.finding: DID NOT FIRE. THE PAIRING HOLDS 2 of 2 for the dispatched sibling agents, and 4 of 4 across every agent that got a reading. Recomputed by my own script (scratchpad/rev_recompute.py), which imports neither hook and does not call the implementer's checker; it re-derives total = input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens over a 1,000,000 window. (1) key ...#a6df3902f0bf72c29 -> wk-alpha; wk-alpha/gauge.json says observed_at 2026-08-06T04:32:19.675Z fill 0.329482; agent-a6df3902f0bf72c29.jsonl holds EXACTLY ONE record at that instant, isSidechain true and agentId == a6df3902f0bf72c29, totalling 329482 tokens = 0.329482. (2) key ...#a69093b8ea2f159f6 -> wk-bravo; observed_at 04:33:30.534Z fill 0.102211; agent-a69093b8ea2f159f6.jsonl holds exactly one record at that instant, 102211 tokens = 0.102211. Plus parent 0.094663 at 04:35:45.657Z from the parent's own non-sidechain records, and depth-2 ECHO 0.064216 at 04:35:11.133Z from agent-acbcb46bdf651a3c7.jsonl. FOUR ANTI-CROSS TESTS, all clean: each gauge's sampled instant appears in NO other agent's transcript and not in the parent's - so no gauge could have been sourced from a different agent. Two further independent cuts I added: every agent-<id>.jsonl carries exactly one distinct agentId (its own) and is entirely isSidechain, so the files cannot be confused; and the counterfactual - a parent-transcript fallback at ALPHA's sampled instant would have read 0.047769, not 0.329482 (at BRAVO's instant, 0.051667, not 0.102211), so the numbers demonstrably did not come from the parent.

f4-observed-at.title: Falsifier 4 — observed_at predates first chunk read
f4-observed-at.imperative: Compare each gauge.json observed_at against that agent's first transcript chunk-read timestamp. FIRES (fail) if a reading predates the agent's own reads (stale or parent-sourced).
f4-observed-at.finding: DID NOT FIRE. My own scan for the earliest Read tool_use in each dispatched agent's own transcript: ALPHA first Read 2026-08-06T04:31:21.087Z, gauge observed_at 04:32:19.675Z (58s later); BRAVO first Read 04:32:59.547Z, observed_at 04:33:30.534Z (31s later). Neither reading predates its agent's own reading. Stronger still, the sandbox gauge.json mtimes are 21:32:20.3, 21:33:31.2, 21:35:11.8 and 21:35:46.3 local (= UTC-7), each landing 0.2-0.6s AFTER the observed_at it carries and interleaved across the live 5-minute run - so the files were written during the run at four different moments, not pre-seeded and not batch-written afterwards (recompute.py did not run until 21:38).

f5-advance-refused.title: Falsifier 5 — advance succeeded despite >= hard
f5-advance-refused.imperative: Confirm the >= hard reading actually refused the advance in the treatment run. FIRES (fail) if advance succeeded.
f5-advance-refused.finding: DID NOT FIRE. Read from the state, not the report: sb-treatment/.agent-work/wk-alpha/spine.json has top-level refusals=1, tasks.g1.status='in-progress' and g2 still 'pending'; its journal contains exactly one entry, verb='start', with no advance entry at all. All three other treatment spines have refusals=0 and g1='complete'. ALPHA's g1 postcondition c1 is 'exit 0' and shows satisfied=false, so the refusal cannot be attributed to a failing check - the only thing that could refuse was the trip. I also pulled the raw tool_result out of ALPHA's own transcript: 'REFUSED: g1: context at 33% is at/over the hard limit ... EXIT_CODE:1'.

f6-control-tripped.title: Falsifier 6 — the control arm also tripped
f6-control-tripped.imperative: Verify the control arm produced no reading for any dispatched agent and advanced normally. FIRES (fail) if control tripped.
f6-control-tripped.finding: DID NOT FIRE. All four sb-control spines: refusals=0, g1='complete'. The control binding store holds ONE bare key (the session uuid) mapping to three spines at once, and the only gauge.json in the whole control arm is wk-parent's frozen 0.047721 sampled at 04:40:53.218Z - i.e. 8 seconds BEFORE the second claim at 04:41:01.733Z, after which the key became ambiguous and the governor went blind. Four gauge-skip.json sidecars record 'ambiguous-binding' with candidate_count 3 and 4. Zero readings for any dispatched agent.

f7-verbatim.title: Falsifier 7 — a reported output is paraphrased
f7-verbatim.imperative: Spot-check reported outputs in the implementer result against the raw evidence files byte-for-byte. FIRES (fail) on paraphrase presented as verbatim.
f7-verbatim.finding: DID NOT FIRE. I re-extracted the engine commands and their raw tool_results directly from ALPHA and BRAVO own transcripts with my own parser and compared them to the blocks quoted in the implementer result. ALPHA CONTEXT 12% (>= soft), CONTEXT 27% (>= hard) and the REFUSED: g1: context at 33% ... EXIT_CODE:1 block all match exactly, including the trailing EXIT_CODE:1 marker - which I checked was NOT injected by the prompt (grep for EXIT_CODE, EXITCODE and LASTEXITCODE across both prompts and make_prompts.py returns nothing); ALPHA appended a literal semicolon-echo EXIT_CODE-dollar-question-mark suffix to that one command on its own initiative. BRAVO CONTEXT 9% (>= soft) and g1 -> complete match my extraction too. Nothing is paraphrased. [Supersedes my previous recording of this item, where the shell expanded the dollar-question-mark before the engine saw it.]

f8-harness-provenance.title: Falsifier 8 — an identity value traces to the harness
f8-harness-provenance.imperative: Reproduce the 7-pattern grep over the acceptance path AND the set-difference proof that the session dir and all five agent transcripts were harness-created. Additionally rule out a pre-seeded binding file, a hand-made subagents/agent-<hex>.jsonl, and an environment variable. FIRES (fail) if any identity value can be traced to the harness rather than the payload.
f8-harness-provenance.finding: DID NOT FIRE, and I did not rely on the implementer grep. I ran a broader sweep of my own design: every file under scratchpad/accept419 whose mtime predates the counted session start (21:31:06 local), excluding run-1 and smoke artifacts - 71 files, more than double the 32 the implementer walked - grepped for agent_id, agentId, each of the five agent ids the run produced, and the session uuid prefix e0063a6f. Every pattern returned 0 files. The three evasions the handoff named are each closed separately. (a) PRE-SEEDED BINDING FILE: the sandbox binding store did not exist before the run (prerun-empty.txt) and its live mtime is 21:35:15, mid-run; the ids it contains are the run-2 ids. (b) HAND-MADE agent-<hex>.jsonl: the run-2 session dir e0063a6f is NOT in the pre-run set (which held only run-1 session b9e77515 and memory), so the session dir, its subagents/ directory and all five agent-*.jsonl were created by the harness during the run - I confirmed the set difference myself on disk, and confirmed the five run-1 agent ids (a155bf.., a1f9a2.., a2ece0.., ab7d5c.., ac1456..) are disjoint from the five run-2 ids. The transcripts are 32KB-910KB of real model turns with per-turn usage blocks and matching .meta.json files; each carries exactly one agentId, its own. (c) ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE: neither settings file has an env block, neither launch command sets one, and grep for CLAUDE_, "env", setx and $env: across both settings, both launch commands, both prompts, build_sandbox.py and make_prompts.py returns nothing. I also confirmed the prompts never mention trip, gauge, hard, soft, band, fill, refusal or any target number - the agents were not coached.

c1-trip-recomputed.title: Close criterion 1 — trip fired from a per-agent reading, re-computed by me
c1-trip-recomputed.imperative: Verify a HARD trip fired from a per-agent reading on a live run, by YOUR re-computation from the raw transcripts, not from the harness report. Record pass/fail.
c1-trip-recomputed.finding: MET, by my own re-computation. A HARD trip fired on a live run from a reading that is provably ALPHA own. My parser (not the hook, not the implementer checker) recomputes 329482 tokens over the 1M sonnet-5 window = 0.329482 from the single record at 2026-08-06T04:32:19.675Z in agent-a6df3902f0bf72c29.jsonl, and that is byte-for-byte the fill_fraction in wk-alpha/gauge.json. The refusal is in the state, not just the report: wk-alpha refusals=1, g1 in-progress, journal holds only a start entry. ALPHA own transcript shows the reading MOVING across its run - 12% then 27% then 33% at three separate engine calls - which no frozen, parent-sourced or fabricated value could do. I also re-ran the implementer recompute.py: exit 0, output byte-identical to the archived copy.

c2-parent-and-release.title: Close criterion 2 — parent bare key, release scoped, non-claimer silent
c2-parent-and-release.imperative: Verify the parent held exactly one bare-key entry and got its own reading; a release removed that agent's composite key while the parent's survived; the non-claiming subagent wrote nothing. Record pass/fail.
c2-parent-and-release.finding: MET, all four halves. (1) PARENT: exactly one bare key in the store, holding exactly one spine, wk-parent - and it got its own reading, 0.094663, which I recomputed from the parent own non-sidechain transcript records at 04:35:45.657Z. Its gauge carries only the four required fields, no identity_resolution_ms, so the top-level record shape is unchanged. (2) RELEASE: ECHO released (wk-echo engine_session status=released, journal shows start then advance) and there is NO composite key ending in acbcb46bdf651a3c7 anywhere in the store, while the parent bare key survived that release - I read the store directly. (3) NON-CLAIMER: CHARLIE (a44094d0026a4e495) has no key in the store, and a find over the whole treatment sandbox returns exactly four gauge files, one per claimed spine, with no fifth directory and no stray sidecar. (4) DELTA, which dispatched ECHO but claimed nothing itself, likewise bound nothing.

c3-identity-path-recorded.title: Close criterion 3 — identity path and resolved key shape recorded
c3-identity-path-recorded.imperative: Verify the run recorded which identity path it took and the resolved key shape, so a silent fallback could not have passed. Record pass/fail.
c3-identity-path-recorded.finding: MET, with a caveat about how it is recorded. The resolved key shape is recorded directly and unambiguously in the binding store: two keys of shape <session-uuid>#<agent-hex> alongside one bare <session-uuid>, so a silent fallback to the bare-key path would have left three spines under one bare key exactly as the control arm did - the two shapes are visibly different states, not the same state with different labels. Which path each record took is recorded by the presence or absence of identity_resolution_ms: it rides ONLY the three dispatched-agent records (0.08370, 0.07760, 0.08050 ms, all inside the 100ms budget) and is absent from the parent record. So the field doubles as a per-record marker of the dispatched-identity path, which is what makes the claim checkable. CAVEAT worth naming: this is an inference from a timing field, not an explicit path label such as source=payload-agent-id. It is sufficient here because the alternative path is directly observable in the same evidence (the control arm), but a future run without a control arm would have less to lean on.

c4-nested-depth2.title: Close criterion 4 — nested depth-2 result recorded and true
c4-nested-depth2.imperative: Verify the nested depth-2 dispatch's identity actually resolved, from raw evidence. If it did not, the governor is silently blind for nested agents. Record pass/fail either way.
c4-nested-depth2.finding: MET and INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: the depth-2 dispatch RESOLVED. I read agent-acbcb46bdf651a3c7.meta.json directly: spawnDepth 2, parentAgentId a3ab804c97222f9c5 (DELTA). Its transcript sits directly under the ROOT session subagents/ directory, NOT under DELTA - which is precisely why derive_subagent_transcript, which builds <parent-transcript-minus-.jsonl>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl from the ROOT transcript path, resolves at depth 2 at all. wk-echo/gauge.json holds 0.064216 at 04:35:11.133Z; the single record at that instant in agent-acbcb46bdf651a3c7.jsonl totals 64216 tokens, isSidechain true, agentId its own, and that instant appears in no other transcript. This is a genuinely new fact - the pre-build probe only ever captured spawnDepth 1 - and it is the good outcome: the governor is NOT blind for nested agents. Note the pairing survived even though ECHO composite key had already been removed by its own release, so I recomputed it from the spine directory rather than through the store.

c5-control-arm.title: Close criterion 5 — control arm silent and byte-identical script
c5-control-arm.imperative: Verify the control arm ran the byte-identical script against unmodified main hooks, produced no dispatched-agent reading, and advanced normally. Diff the two prompt/script inputs yourself. Record pass/fail.
c5-control-arm.finding: MET, and the control is cleaner than the report claims. I diffed the two prompts myself normalising ONLY the sandbox directory name (sb-treatment -> sb-control): diff exits 0, so the script the agents followed is byte-identical between arms. I diffed the two settings files normalising only the hook directory: exit 0. Crucially, I checked which engine each arm names and BOTH prompts point at the SAME checklist_engine.py, the worktree one - so the trip implementation is held constant and the only variable in the whole experiment is which directory the two PostToolUse hook scripts are loaded from. I verified the control hook directory is genuinely unmodified: C:/Programs/constellation-skills is on main at 990712f, clean, and both its hook files differ from the worktree copies (main spine_rail.py has no binding_key function at all). Result: zero readings for any dispatched agent in the control arm, four ambiguous-binding sidecars, every g1 complete, refusals=0 on all four spines. The control gauge pipeline was demonstrably ALIVE, not merely absent - the control parent got one reading, 0.047721, sampled 8 seconds before the second claim made the bare key ambiguous - so the silence is the pre-fix blindness, not a broken control.

d1-run1-discard.title: Disclosure 1 — discarded treatment run 1
d1-run1-discard.imperative: Check the counted run is genuinely the re-run, that nothing from run 1 leaked into the counted evidence, and that discarding run 1 was honest rather than convenient. Record pass/fail with a finding.
d1-run1-discard.finding: HONEST, and the discard cost the implementer evidence rather than buying it. The counted run is genuinely the re-run: the counted binding store carries session e0063a6f-5f31-473e-938a-1feea2863166, whose session directory was created 21:31:06 local, while run 1 session b9e77515 ran 21:23-21:28 and its whole sandbox was moved to accept419/run1/ before the counted sandbox was regenerated (corpus mtimes 21:30:16). The two runs five agent ids are disjoint sets. Grepping the entire counted evidence tree for b9e77515 returns only two files, and in both it is named legitimately as a pre-existing artifact (prerun-empty.txt records it as the before-set; agentid-grep.txt enumerates the walked path). No leak. On honesty: I read run 1 archived spines. Run 1 ALREADY had the win - wk-alpha refusals=1, g1 in-progress, gauge 0.332189, composite key ...#ab7d5c3b6d5c61865 present. It was discarded because wk-bravo and wk-echo were never even started (g1 pending, no refusals field), which meant no second dispatched agent, hence no pairing count and no distinct-fills falsifier. Discarding it made the bar HARDER, not easier. Bonus finding the implementer did not claim: the HARD trip therefore fired in TWO independent runs, with different session uuids, different agent ids and different fills (0.332189 and 0.329482) - an unplanned replication.

d2-classifier-recovery.title: Disclosure 2 — transcript-recovered agent report
d2-classifier-recovery.imperative: Judge whether substituting transcript-recovered commands/results for a classifier-blocked authored report is stronger (no agent wrote it) or weaker (selected after the fact by the reviewed party). Verify the recovered material against the raw transcript yourself. Record pass/fail with a finding.
d2-classifier-recovery.finding: STRONGER, not weaker - and I verified it rather than taking the argument on trust. The concern is real: material selected after the fact by the party being reviewed is normally weaker evidence. What defeats the concern here is that the selection is checkable and I checked it. I wrote my own extractor over BRAVO raw transcript agent-a69093b8ea2f159f6.jsonl, pulling every checklist_engine tool_use and its paired tool_result, and it reproduces exactly what the implementer reported: two current calls, the second ending CONTEXT 9% (>= soft), and an advance returning g1 -> complete. Nothing was omitted and nothing was added; the archived g4-commands-treatment.txt carries the same strings. The substitution is stronger than an authored report for the reason given - a tool_result is a machine record no agent composed, so it cannot be paraphrased or flattered - and the selection risk is neutralised because the raw transcript is archived alongside it, so any reviewer can redo the extraction, as I did. Note the classifier refusal hit BRAVO FINAL MESSAGE only, after all its tool calls had completed, so no observation was lost - its claim, both current calls, its advance, its gauge and its spine journal all exist.

a1-null-hypothesis.title: Adversarial — explain the trip WITHOUT the change
a1-null-hypothesis.imperative: Enumerate every way the observed trip could occur in a world where the change did nothing (parent reading leaking to child, harness-authored gauge, shared spine dir, control arm mis-wired, corpus size alone). Try to construct each and show it fails against the evidence. Record pass/fail with a finding.
a1-null-hypothesis.finding: I could not construct any world in which the change did nothing and this evidence still looks like this. Nine attempts, each killed by evidence I reproduced. (1) PARENT READING LEAKED INTO A CHILD SPINE: the parent transcript at ALPHA sampled instant reads 0.047769, not 0.329482 - a 7x gap. (2) HARNESS WROTE THE GAUGE FILES: the four gauge mtimes land 0.2-0.6s after the four different observed_at values they carry, spread across a 5-minute window during which the implementer process was blocked on the claude -p call (out-treatment.txt not written until 21:36); recompute.py did not exist until 21:38. To fake this the implementer would have had to know each agent token total in real time. (3) CONTROL ARM MIS-WIRED SO IT COULD NOT TRIP: both arms name the same checklist_engine.py, so the trip code is identical; and the control gauge pipeline demonstrably worked - it produced a parent reading and four ambiguous-binding sidecars. (4) CONTROL AGENTS SIMPLY READ LESS: control ALPHA independently reached 0.329265 against treatment ALPHA 0.329482, a 0.02% difference, and got no reading and a clean advance. (5) CORPUS SIZE ALONE CAUSES THE TRIP: refuted by (4). (6) A STALE OR PRE-EXISTING GAUGE: the sandbox binding store and every gauge file were absent before the run, and each observed_at postdates its agent first Read by 31-58s. (7) THE TWO FILLS ARE ONE NUMBER SAMPLED TWICE: 0.329482 vs 0.102211. (8) A CROSSED PAIRING THAT STILL LOOKS RIGHT: four independent anti-cross tests - each gauge sampled instant is unique to one transcript - plus every agent-<id>.jsonl carrying exactly one agentId, its own. (9) THE AGENTS WERE COACHED: the prompts never contain the words trip, gauge, hard, soft, band, fill or refusal, nor any target number. WHAT REMAINS UNTESTED, stated plainly: one platform, one model, sequential dispatch only, one counted run (replicated once by the discarded run 1); concurrent claims against the unlocked binding store are a real untested property the implementer already filed as a triage candidate.

triage_candidates.statement: g4-assert-control-output.txt does not reproduce from g4-assert_control.py: the archived output carries a trailing 8-line section (what the control arm agents ACTUALLY consumed) that the archived script has no code to emit, so it was appended from an unrecorded command. Every number in it independently reproduces, so nothing is wrong with the claim - but an evidence file that cannot be regenerated from its own archived script is a hygiene defect. Fix: fold the section into the script, or head it with the command that produced it.

docs/GAUGE_WRITER_HOOK.md carries nothing about nested dispatch, yet g4 established a durable new fact: a depth-2 agent transcript is written directly under the ROOT session subagents/ directory (spawnDepth 2, parentAgentId set in its .meta.json), which is why derive_subagent_transcript resolves at depth 2. Route to Cartographer so the doc records the depth-2 behavior as observed rather than unknown.

The archived acceptance harness re-derives the arm concept (arm name, sandbox dir, settings file, prompt file, ~/.claude/projects slug) in each of its five scripts, which is why check() and slug_for() are duplicated and why a sandbox-layout change would touch all five files. Only worth doing if a second live-acceptance run is planned.

Carry forward the implementer own triage candidate and raise its priority: the binding store is read-modify-write on one JSON file with no cross-process lock, and the per-agent keying makes a wave write N entries where it used to write one. g4 deliberately dispatched sequentially, so this is untested. A lost write means that agent silently gets no reading - the exact blindness this issue set out to remove.
